mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 m/m change < -1% AND HOUST m/m change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12mo MA AND UNRATE stable (|UNRATE - 12mo MA| < 0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 returns exists in the post-2015 period; when INDPRO rises month-over-month, S&P 500 tends to rise over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO m/m > 0% but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of cases.
